entry.title: Your baby’s daily rhythm
entry.summary: The authors look for a baby’s changing rhythm of feeding, play and sleep, with familiar cues for transitions. Their pattern is a guide to noticing, not a timetable.
entry.cue: You are trying to understand what your baby needs next.
detail: Their usual wake–feed–play–sleep sequence varies as the baby grows. Sometimes play comes before a feed, and travel or changes at home can shift what is familiar.
A repeated phrase or song can signal what is coming. The authors suggest coordinating with other caregivers where possible, while keeping the baby’s own cues in view.

Family rituals can be part of that familiar world too: a regular park visit, a special breakfast or a celebration from one or more family cultures. The baby can be included before they can contribute much themselves.

references.locator: Variable infant rhythm, familiar transition cues and optional family rituals

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
